Subject: Re: Order form redlines — indemnity questions

Marcus —

Thanks for sending the draft order form. A couple things jumped out from our procurement & privacy teams:

- We cannot accept unilateral right-to-defend where Redwood assumes full control for IP claims tied to customer data or customer-provided models/fine-tuning data.
- For EU customers we have regulatory concerns if defense control impedes our ability to coordinate with our local counsel and regulators.
- We need clearer notice/cure windows and an explicit carveout for claims that arise solely from our customer-uploaded training data.

I attached our redlines (Nebula_Redlines_v1.pdf) with inline comments. Can Redwood suggest concrete language we can route to our counsel?

Thanks,

Nebula Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Order form redlines — indemnity questions

Celine — appreciate the redlines and the clear callouts. Attaching our working counter (Redwood_hybrid-indemnity-draft.docx). High-level proposal from Redwood to move the conversation forward:

1) Hybrid defend/reimburse split: Redwood will accept defense control for third-party IP claims that are caused solely by Redwood-owned model weights, training pipeline, or our published model derivatives.
2) Customer-responsibility carveout: Claims arising from customer inputs (uploaded datasets, prompts, fine-tuning datasets, or customer-supplied models) would instead be subject to reimbursement (or customer defense control) — effectively the customer would defend/indemnify Redwood for those claims.
3) EU-specific accommodation: for Nebula EU customers, Redwood is willing to a) limit our defense control to technical areas where Redwood logs and audit trails can demonstrate non-involvement, and b) accept a lower monetary cap in EU (see proposal below) if Nebula agrees to enhanced logging/retention on your side or to use Redwood Dedicated for the workload.
4) Notice & cure: 15-day notice to Redwood from receipt of third-party claim; 30-day cure period where feasible.
5) Caps: propose $5M aggregate worldwide, with $2M carveout cap applicable for EU-resident customers (negotiable).

We believe this balances operational efficacy (we can run the defense where our engineers and model logs are required) and your regulatory concerns.

Next step: Kimberly and Jordan — see the attached draft legal language for defend/reimburse split and flag any material procurement blockers. Celine — can you share the Nebula redline doc and a primary counsel contact?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

On Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:

Marcus / Celine —

Thanks — I reviewed Marcus's proposed split and added clarifying edits. Key legal points in the attached KR_redlines_comments.docx:

- Right to defend: Redwood will accept defense control for eligible claims, but only where Redwood: (i) receives timely written notice; (ii) has exclusive control over the defense and settlement of the claim; and (iii) the claim does not arise from Nebula-provided content (including datasets and prompt libraries).
- Cooperation: Nebula must reasonably cooperate (provide evidence, access to logs, testimony). We can't assume responsibility where Nebula's data or configurations caused the alleged infringement.
- Reservation of rights: Redwood reserves the right to participate in the defense at its expense where Nebula elects to defend.
- Allocation: If a claim derives from both Redwood and Nebula actions, parties will reasonably allocate defense costs based on relative fault.
- EU nuances: recommend a small EU-specific carveout: require a negotiated escalation path with local counsel and a limited reimbursement fallback where EU law prevents exclusive defense control.

I'll flag two areas procurement will push back on: (a) the allocation language is standard but customers dislike open-ended apportionment terms; (b) caps and insurance offsets — we should decide a negotiating floor.

-Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

On Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800, Oliver Mendes <oliver.mendes@nebulahealth.com> wrote:

Kimberly / Marcus —

Appreciate the clarity. From legal/regulatory: the EU fallback is the sticking point. Nebula's counsel will not accept any clause that allows Redwood to unilaterally exclude Nebula counsel or delay regulatory notification in a way that would breach local GDPR/controller obligations. They asked for: mutual defense for EU claims OR a clear reimbursement mechanism tied to documented legal fees and settlements.

We can accept defend where: (i) Redwood provides evidence (audit logs) proving the claim is not from our uploaded data, and (ii) Nebula maintains the right to instruct local counsel for regulatory interactions.

Oliver Mendes
General Counsel (EMEA)
Nebula Health

On Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:30:00 -0800, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:

Celine / Oliver / Kimberly / Jordan —

Thanks for the candid feedback. We've pulled everything together and propose a concrete set of revisions that I think are a practical compromise for both sides (see summary below and updated doc attached in HubSpot):

- Definition: "Redwood-Responsible Claim" = third-party claim alleging IP infringement where the only plausible causal chain is Redwood's model weights, training process, or published model artifacts (explicitly excludes customer uploads, prompts, and fine-tuned models).
- Defense Control: Redwood will defend Redwood-Responsible Claims at our expense and with primary control of litigation, provided Nebula gives timely written notice and reasonable cooperation.
- Customer-Input Claims: If the claim reasonably arises from Nebula-provided data or configuration, Nebula will have first right to defend; Redwood will reimburse documented defense costs and settlements up to a reimbursement limit.
- EU accommodation: For Nebula EU-resident customers, where local law precludes exclusive control, parties will default to a mutual-defense approach with proportional cost allocation. As a commercial concession, Redwood will reduce the EU monetary cap to $2,000,000 aggregate for this order and offer to enable Redwood Dedicated (audit logs + retention) at a discounted add-on to support forensic needs.
- Notice & Cure: 15 days notice; 30 days for cure/engagement; where urgent regulators are involved, parties will coordinate on accelerated timelines.
- Caps & Insurance: $5,000,000 worldwide aggregate cap; $2,000,000 EU-specific cap for this order. Each party represents it has commercial insurance; standard insurance-offsets apply.

If you can confirm the commercial terms above (caps & Dedicated as mitigation), we will produce finalized legal language and route the order form for signature. I can also open a DocuSign envelope (link above) when counsel confirms the language.

Action items:
- Nebula: confirm whether the EU mutual-defense fallback plus $2M EU cap is acceptable, and share your primary counsel contact.
- Redwood Legal (Kimberly / Jordan): convert the summary into final redline language for the order form; propose negotiation floor for caps if needed.
- Sales Ops: tag this deal in HubSpot under NBH-9234 and prepare a pricing attachment for Redwood Dedicated (discounted audit logs).

Thanks all — happy to jump on a quick call this week to close.

Best,
